transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I've been having some trouble at work. At the register, I keep getting stuck doing things that just don't fit the moment. Like, I'll start tapping the scanner in a pattern. It's one of those laser scanners, you know? The red light on it always reminds me of the tail lights on my old Ford Taurus. I drove that car all the way to Omaha back in the nineties. The highway out there is just endlessly flat, and the sky gets so big... I used to love driving like that, just listening to the radio fade in and out. 

But anyway, I also end up just freezing with my hand hovering right over the open cash drawer while the customer is standing there waiting for their change. It actually got me written up last week. My manager used a blue pen to sign the write-up, which I thought was strange because he usually insists on black ink for official company forms. He's very particular about office supplies, especially the staples.
Do you find yourself doing things like tapping the scanner in a pattern often?

Yeah, like I was saying, it happens a lot. That's exactly why I'm here. I just keep getting stuck doing those things that don't fit the moment, over and over. Tapping the scanner, or just freezing completely with my hand hovering right over the open cash drawer while the customer is just... staring at me, waiting for their change. It happens enough that it got me that write-up last week. 

But you know, that cash drawer actually gets physically stuck sometimes, too. The metal rollers on the tracks are completely rusted out. You'd think corporate could afford a single can of WD-40. My dad used to keep a can of that on the workbench in the garage for absolutely everything. Squeaky hinge? WD-40. Rusted bolt? WD-40. He actually sprayed it all over the engine block of his riding mower once because he thought it would make the blades spin faster. It smoked up the entire cul-de-sac. Mrs. Gable next door thought the garage was burning down and called the fire department. They sent two whole trucks just for a lawnmower...
Do you find yourself tapping things in patterns or getting stuck on repetitive behaviors when you're not at work?

When I'm not at work? Um... no, not really. I don't think I do it at home. Just at the store, mostly. I mean, at home I'm usually just watching TV. Although I do mess with the remote sometimes because it's broken. The little plastic tab on the battery door snapped off last month, so I have to keep the batteries in with a thick rubber band. 

But rubber bands dry out so fast, you know? They get all brittle and just snap if you stretch them even a little bit. I used to keep a whole ball of them in my desk drawer when I was in college. I spent four years making this giant rubber band ball, it was about the size of a grapefruit by the time I actually got my degree. I wonder what happened to that thing. I think I might have left it in my dorm room when I moved out. Room 214. The radiator in that room clanked all winter long, sounded exactly like someone hitting a lead pipe with a wrench. It drove my roommate absolutely crazy, but I kind of liked the rhythm of it. He ended up moving out halfway through the semester to live with his girlfriend off-campus.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to focus on something else?

Thoughts repeating? Um... no, I don't really think so. My mind doesn't really get stuck on thoughts like that. Well, unless you count getting a song stuck in your head, like that old carpet cleaning commercial jingle from the eighties. They used to play it constantly during the daytime soap operas. My grandmother used to watch Days of Our Lives every single afternoon, right at 1:00 PM. You couldn't call her or interrupt her when it was on. She had this massive floral armchair that smelled exactly like peppermint and mothballs, and she'd just sit there with her cup of Earl Grey tea. She always spilled a little bit, so there was this permanent brown ring stained into the saucer. I actually tried to buy that exact same brand of tea at the store the other day, but they completely redesigned the boxes. They made them all shiny and modern-looking, which just feels wrong for hot tea, you know? It should look classic, like it's been around forever. The new cardboard they use feels really cheap, too, like it would just fall apart if it got even a little bit damp.
Do you have trouble talking to people or making friends?

Um... talking to people? I don't know, I still care about my wife and kids, obviously. But I just don't really have the push to... do much with anyone lately. Like, I don't even call my son at college, or go out with my kayak group anymore. I used to go out on the river with them every other weekend. We'd put in down by the old steel mill. That mill shut down back in the nineties, I think. It's just a bunch of rusted-out buildings now, but the city was supposed to turn it into a park. They put up all these chain-link fences with those green privacy screens, but the wind just tears them to shreds. You see those green strips flapping around everywhere when it storms. 

But yeah, even my little repair projects in the garage... I just don't have the drive for it. And when people ask me what's wrong, I mostly just shrug. I can't really find much to say. Words just kind of... don't come. Kind of like when the spark plugs go bad on a weed whacker. You pull and pull the cord, and it just sputters and dies. I bought this cheap generic brand of spark plugs online once, thinking I was saving a few bucks, but they were completely useless. The threading was all wrong, so it wouldn't even seat properly in the engine block. I ended up having to take the whole thing apart on the workbench, which was a mess because I had just reorganized all my socket wrenches. I have this red metal toolbox with the drawers that slide out, but the bottom drawer always gets stuck if you put too much weight in it...
Do you have any thoughts that you feel compelled to think about over and over?

Compelled to think about over and over? No, I don't... I don't think I have anything like that. Just the normal stuff, you know? Like if I forgot to take the trash out. The garbage truck comes so early now, they changed the route a few months ago. It used to be they'd come around noon, which was perfect because I could just wheel the bin out after I woke up. But now it's like 6:00 AM, and the brakes on that truck squeal so loud. It sounds exactly like the brakes on my old '98 sedan right before I finally had to get the rotors replaced. The mechanic tried to tell me I needed new calipers too, but I knew he was just trying to upcharge me. You have to watch out for those guys, they'll show you a dirty air filter that isn't even from your car just to get an extra thirty bucks out of you. My dad taught me how to check my own air filters when I was a teenager. We used to spend every Sunday afternoon in the driveway, just tinkering with his truck. He had this old Ford, painted this really ugly mustard yellow color...
Do you have any thoughts that you feel are intrusive or unwanted?

Intrusive thoughts? Unwanted? Um... no, I don't really get things popping into my head that I don't want there. My brain just kind of does its own thing, mostly pretty quiet. Well, except when the store gets really busy. I work a register, and when the line backs up past the frozen food aisle, it gets so loud in there. The beep of the scanner just echoes. It's a really specific pitch, too, almost like a microwave when it's done, but sharper. Our microwave at home has this really annoying beep, and the button to open the door is starting to stick. You have to press it right in the top left corner or it won't pop open. I tried spraying a little WD-40 in the latch mechanism, but it just made the whole kitchen smell like oil for three days. My wife was not happy about that. She ended up opening all the windows, even though it was freezing outside. We have those old wooden window frames, and they swell up in the winter, so once you open them, getting them to shut again is a real chore. I had to use a rubber mallet to tap the sash back down into place.
Do you find it enjoyable to spend time with your family and friends?

Enjoyable? I mean... I guess I still care about my wife and kids, you know, obviously. But enjoyable isn't really the word. I just don't have the push to do much with them lately. Like I said before, I don't even call my son at college. And my kayak group, I haven't met up with them in forever. I don't even have the drive to work on my little repair projects in the garage anymore. When people ask what's wrong, I mostly just shrug because I can't really find much to say. It's just... flat. Like when you open a can of soda and leave it on the counter overnight. My wife drinks that diet cherry stuff, and she always leaves half-empty cans sitting around. The aluminum gets this weird sticky ring on the bottom that stains the Formica countertops. We have those old countertops from the seventies, the ones with the little gold flecks in them. They look like someone spilled glitter into the glue. I tried scrubbing the stains out with baking soda and vinegar once, because I saw it on this home improvement show. The guy on the show had this really thick Boston accent, he kept calling the sink a "zink." He was rebuilding this whole Victorian house by himself. Those old Victorians have so much hidden rot in the walls, though. You pull down the plaster and find out the studs are basically just dust...
Do you find yourself being very particular about details or having a strong need for order and symmetry in your daily life?

Particular about details? Order and symmetry? No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really care if things are lined up perfectly or whatever. I mean, my side of the closet is a mess. I just throw my work shirts wherever. They're these awful polo shirts, bright blue with the company logo embroidered on the pocket. The threading on the logo is really stiff, and it scratches right against your chest if you don't wear an undershirt. I always buy those cheap packs of white t-shirts to wear underneath, but they shrink so much in the wash. After two washes, they barely tuck into your pants anymore. And our washing machine is terrible anyway, it's always off-balance during the spin cycle. It bangs against the wall so hard the whole laundry room shakes. It actually knocked a picture frame off the shelf above it last week. It was this old picture from a family trip to the Grand Canyon when the kids were little. The glass shattered everywhere, and I had to sweep it up. Sweeping glass is the worst because you never get all those tiny little slivers. I was finding them with my bare feet for days. It reminds me of when I was a kid and stepped on a bee at the park. My foot swelled up like a balloon...
Do you have any thoughts that feel like they're forcing you to think about them, even if you don't want to?

Forcing me to think about them? No, not really. Like I said before, my brain is mostly just quiet. It kind of just drifts along on its own. The only thing that really forces me to think is when they change the PLU codes at work. They just updated the system for the produce section, and they changed the code for the organic bananas. It used to be so easy to remember, just a four-digit number, but now you have to punch in this whole long sequence. Bananas are always the biggest seller, especially on Sunday mornings. People come in right after church to get their groceries for the week. The church down the street from our house has these massive bells that ring right at noon. You can hear them all the way from our backyard. We tried to set up a little patio out there last summer, bought one of those metal fire pits from the hardware store. It rusted out after the very first rain, though. The metal was so cheap and thin, you could practically bend it with your bare hands. I tried to take it back to get a refund, but I'd already thrown away the receipt. The guy at the returns desk was really rude about it, too. He had this little mustache that looked like it was drawn on with a permanent marker, and he just kept tapping his pen on the counter while I was talking...
Do you feel a strong urge to perform specific rituals or routines in your daily life?

Rituals? Like... having to do things a certain way every time? No, I don't really have anything like that. I just sort of get up and go to work. The morning routine is pretty standard, I guess. I make coffee, but I don't even care how it's made anymore. We have one of those drip machines that takes forever. It gurgles and spits water everywhere because the filter basket is slightly warped. I tried to bend it back into shape, but it's that cheap plastic that just snaps if you push too hard. Plastic is in everything now. I was reading a magazine in the breakroom the other day, and there was this whole article about how microplastics are in the rain. Imagine that, it rains plastic. The breakroom at work always smells like burnt popcorn, too. There's this one guy, Gary, he works the deli counter, and he always puts his popcorn in the microwave for exactly three and a half minutes. It always burns. Every single time. And he just eats it anyway. He sits there reading the sports section, crunching on these black, charred pieces of popcorn. The sports section is getting so thin lately, anyway. The whole newspaper is. My dad used to get the Sunday paper, and it was thick enough to use as a doorstop. He'd sit in his recliner all afternoon reading it. That recliner was this awful olive green color, corduroy. If you sat in it wearing shorts, the ridges would leave these deep red lines all up and down the backs of your legs...
Do you ever have thoughts that keep coming back into your mind, even when you try to think about something else?

Thoughts that keep coming back? Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't get stuck on things like that. My mind just sort of wanders from one thing to the next, you know? Like when I'm scanning items, I just look at the barcodes. Some of the barcodes are really hard to scan because the ink is smeared. The frozen food boxes are the worst for that because they get condensation on them when people leave them in their carts too long. It drips all over the belt, and then I have to wipe it down with those paper towels they give us. The paper towels are so rough, they feel like sandpaper. I used to use sandpaper a lot when I was trying to build a birdhouse with my son. He was maybe eight or nine. We bought this kit from the craft store, but none of the pieces fit together right. The wood was all warped. We ended up using half a bottle of wood glue just to get the roof to stay on. Wood glue has such a distinct smell, kind of sweet but also chemical. It reminds me of the smell of the floor wax they use at the supermarket. They always wax the floors on Tuesday nights after we close. You have to be careful walking out to your car because the parking lot lights are on a timer, and half the time they shut off before we're even out the door. It gets pitch black out there, especially in the winter when the sun goes down so early...
Do you find it very difficult to adapt when your routine or plans are changed unexpectedly?

Adapt to changes? I mean, I don't think so. If things change, they change, I just kind of roll with it. Like, if they change my shift at the store, I just show up when they tell me to. Usually they post the schedule on this corkboard in the breakroom, right next to the time clock. The corkboard is so old, though, it's just crumbling. Every time you pull a pushpin out, a little chunk of cork falls on the floor. They use those cheap clear plastic pushpins, but half of them are missing the plastic part so it's just the metal spike sticking out. I stepped on one once, went right through the sole of my shoe. I was wearing those black non-slip shoes they make us buy. You have to order them from this specific catalog, and they take like three weeks to arrive. The shipping boxes they come in always smell like damp cardboard. I used to save cardboard boxes when we moved into our house, thinking we'd use them for storage in the basement. But the basement flooded our second year there, ruined everything. The water heater just gave out one night. It was this massive rusty tank, probably as old as the house itself. The guy who came to replace it had to cut it into pieces just to get it up the stairs...
Do you find it very upsetting when your daily routine is disrupted or when things are not done in a certain order?

Upsetting? Nah, I don't get upset about things being out of order. It doesn't really matter to me. Like, at the register, people will put their stuff on the belt in whatever order they want. Sometimes they put heavy canned goods right next to the bread, or the raw chicken on top of the fresh produce, and I just scan it however it comes down the line. You have to be careful bagging it, though. We use those really thin plastic bags now, since the paper ones are always out of stock. The handles always stretch out and snap if you put more than two jars of pasta sauce in them. Pasta sauce always stains the plastic Tupperware if you heat it up in the microwave anyway. I have this one container at home that's permanently orange. I tried soaking it in bleach and dish soap, but it didn't do anything. The soap just made the water all cloudy. Our tap water gets really cloudy sometimes anyway, especially in the spring when the city flushes the fire hydrants. They open them up and the water just gushes down the street into the storm drains. There's a storm drain right at the corner of my street, and it always gets clogged with wet leaves. The oak tree in my neighbor's yard drops leaves all year round, it feels like. It's a huge tree, its branches hang right over my driveway, so my windshield is always covered in sap...
Do you ever feel like you're thinking about something over and over again, even when you try to stop?

Thinking over and over? Um, no, I don't think my brain really does that. I don't get stuck on one thought. The only thing that repeats over and over is the music they pipe in at the store. They use this corporate radio station that plays the exact same pop songs every single day at the exact same time. The speaker right above register three is blown out, though, so the bass always sounds really fuzzy, like radio static. Static electricity is so bad in the store during the winter anyway. You touch the metal edge of the conveyor belt and get a shock right up your arm. I started keeping a little bottle of hand lotion in my apron pocket because they say dry skin makes static worse. It's just that cheap pink lotion from the dollar aisle, it smells like artificial cherry. My grandmother used to have this massive cherry tree in her backyard when I was a kid. The birds would always get to the cherries before they were even ripe enough to pick. Starlings, mostly. They travel in those huge flocks that look like a dark cloud moving across the sky, shifting around. I saw a documentary about that once, how they coordinate their movements without running into each other. It was on public television. I still watch public television a lot because I refuse to pay the rates for cable. The cable company keeps sending me these thick envelopes with promotional offers, but they just go straight into the blue recycling bin. The recycling truck comes on Thursdays, but sometimes they skip our street entirely if the garbage men parked too close to the curb...
Do you feel uncomfortable when things are not symmetrical or perfectly aligned?

Symmetrical? No, not really. I don't pay much attention to how things line up. I mean, the candy bars at the checkout are never perfectly aligned anyway. People grab a Snickers and knock the whole row over, and I just leave it like that until the end of my shift. The end of my shift is at 4:00, which is right when the high school down the street lets out, so the bus traffic is just terrible. The yellow buses block the entire intersection by the gas station. That gas station used to have really good coffee, but they switched to this new machine that grinds the beans right there, and it's always broken. It just spits out hot water and grounds everywhere. Coffee grounds are supposed to be good for the soil, though. I tried dumping them in my garden last year to help my tomato plants, but I think it just attracted ants. Thousands of them, just marching right up the stems. I had to buy this heavy-duty bug spray from the hardware store, the kind that comes in a metal canister with a pump handle. The pump handle was painted bright red, but the paint started chipping off the very first day I used it. It left these little red flakes all over my hands. I had to scrub with that gritty orange soap mechanics use just to get it off. Mechanics always charge so much just to look at your car, even if it's something simple like a blown fuse. My dashboard lights went out once, and it turned out to just be a ten-cent fuse, but they still charged me a fifty-dollar diagnostic fee...
Do you feel like you have to follow a specific daily routine or perform certain actions in a precise way to feel comfortable or to prevent something bad from happening?

Specific routine? No, I don't really have anything like that. I just kind of take the day as it comes, you know? I don't have to do things exactly the same way to feel okay. Like, I don't even eat breakfast at the same time every day. Sometimes I'll just grab a granola bar on the way out the door if I'm running late. Those oat and honey bars are okay, but they crumble everywhere as soon as you open the wrapper. You end up with crumbs all over the car seat, and they get stuck right in the seams of the upholstery. My car has that dark gray cloth interior, so you can see every single little crumb and piece of lint. I bought one of those hand vacuums that plugs into the cigarette lighter to try and clean it, but the suction on it is practically non-existent. It just sort of pushes the dirt around. I think the filter is clogged, but it's one of those proprietary filters you have to order special from the manufacturer's website. I hate ordering things online because the shipping costs are just outrageous these days. They charge you fifteen dollars just to send a tiny little cardboard box that weighs two ounces. And then half the time, the delivery driver just throws it on the porch anyway. Last week, they delivered a package to my neighbor across the street by mistake, and it sat on his steps for three days in the rain. The cardboard was completely dissolved by the time he finally picked it up. Rain just ruins everything if it sits out too long. My wooden deck in the backyard is starting to rot in the corners because the water pools up there after a heavy storm. I need to get some of that waterproof sealant and paint it on, but you have to wait for three consecutive days of dry weather to apply it, and we haven't had a stretch like that since August...
Do you have any thoughts that feel like they're intruding into your mind without you wanting them to?

Intruding thoughts? No, I don't get anything like that. My mind is pretty quiet, mostly. Well, except for when I'm trying to sleep and I start thinking about all the things I have to do the next day. I have to go to the bank tomorrow to deposit my paycheck because the mobile deposit app on my phone keeps crashing. It just gives me this spinning loading circle and then goes back to the home screen. My phone is getting pretty old, though, the battery barely holds a charge past lunchtime anymore. I have to carry one of those portable power banks in my backpack just to make it through a shift. The power bank is heavy, too, it feels like carrying a brick around. I bought it at the electronics store in the mall, but that store is closing down next month. Half the mall is empty now, actually. All the anchor stores pulled out, so it's just a bunch of empty storefronts with the metal grates pulled down. They put up these fake window displays with pictures of happy people shopping to try and make it look less depressing, but the posters are all peeling at the corners. The adhesive they use must be really cheap. You can see the yellow glue residue underneath where the paper is curling back. It's the same kind of glue they use on those sticky traps for mice. We had a mouse problem in the breakroom at work last winter, and management just put those sticky traps everywhere instead of calling an exterminator. It was awful, you'd come in to get a cup of water and there'd be a mouse stuck to the floor behind the water cooler...
Do you feel an overwhelming need to repeat certain actions or behaviors?

Repeat things? No, I don't really have an urge to do that. I just do something once and move on. Well, unless I'm at work and the barcode won't scan. Sometimes I have to swipe the same bag of frozen peas across the scanner like five or six times before it finally beeps. The glass on those scanners gets so dirty by the end of my shift. People put their leaky meat packages right on it, and the chicken juice just smears everywhere. Chicken is getting ridiculously expensive, by the way. A lady came through my line yesterday with three packs of chicken breasts and it was almost forty dollars. I remember when I was getting my bachelor's degree, you could buy a whole week's worth of groceries for forty bucks. I majored in history, actually. Not that there are a lot of history factories hiring these days, which is why I'm stuck at the register. The conveyor belt at my lane has this awful squeak. It’s this high-pitched squeal, kind of like a loose fan belt on a truck. My neighbor across the alley has this old beat-up Chevy that squeals exactly like that every single morning at 5:30. He just lets it idle in his driveway for twenty minutes before he leaves. The exhaust fumes drift right into my bedroom window if I leave it cracked open. I try to leave it open to get some fresh air, but the window screen is getting completely coated in this greasy black soot. You can't even wash it off with regular dish soap, it just smears the grease around the wire mesh...
Do you ever feel like you must perform a specific action or set of actions in order to feel right or to prevent something bad from happening?

Perform a specific action? No, not really. I don't have to do anything special to feel right or anything like that. I just do what I need to do and that's it. Unless you count trying to get the key into my front door lock. It’s been sticking for months, so you have to jiggle it just right and pull the handle up at the exact same time, otherwise it won't turn. I’ve been meaning to spray some WD-40 in there, but I keep forgetting to buy it. I was at the hardware store last weekend looking for a replacement washer for my bathroom faucet, but the plumbing aisle was a complete disaster. Everything was in the wrong bins, and there was nobody around to help. Hardware stores are impossible to navigate now. They used to have people who actually knew how to fix things, but now it’s just teenagers who point vaguely toward aisle 12. And aisle 12 is always just lightbulbs anyway. I bought a pack of those new LED bulbs because they say they last for ten years, but the light they give off is so weird and harsh. It makes my living room look like an interrogation room or a hospital waiting area. The chairs in the hospital waiting area where my dad was before he passed were that awful vinyl material that sticks to the back of your legs if you wear shorts. It was the middle of July and the air conditioning in that wing was completely broken. They had these big industrial fans set up in the hallways, but all they did was blow the hot air around and drown out the TV. They had the TV tuned to some daytime talk show, but the volume was muted and the closed captions were lagging behind by like three minutes, so you’d see someone crying and the text at the bottom would be talking about a recipe for potato salad...

doctor.intent: determine presence of repetitive behaviors outside of work
doctor.question: Do you find yourself tapping things in patterns or getting stuck on repetitive behaviors when you're not at work?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the repetitive behaviors (tapping, freezing) occur outside of work. The symptom profile for S022 describes these behaviors happening at work (at the register), but does not specify whether they happen when not at work.

patient.answer:
When I'm not at work? Um... no, not really. I don't think I do it at home. Just at the store, mostly. I mean, at home I'm usually just watching TV. Although I do mess with the remote sometimes because it's broken. The little plastic tab on the battery door snapped off last month, so I have to keep the batteries in with a thick rubber band. 

But rubber bands dry out so fast, you know? They get all brittle and just snap if you stretch them even a little bit. I used to keep a whole ball of them in my desk drawer when I was in college. I spent four years making this giant rubber band ball, it was about the size of a grapefruit by the time I actually got my degree. I wonder what happened to that thing. I think I might have left it in my dorm room when I moved out. Room 214. The radiator in that room clanked all winter long, sounded exactly like someone hitting a lead pipe with a wrench. It drove my roommate absolutely crazy, but I kind of liked the rhythm of it. He ended up moving out halfway through the semester to live with his girlfriend off-campus.

doctor.question: Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to focus on something else?
